# Burnticker — settlement coverage

<!-- Generated by `node --import ./test/alias-hook.mjs scripts/burnticker-coverage-audit.mts --offline --write`. Do not edit by hand: change the sources, the taxonomy or the audit, then regenerate. -->

**The rule.** A coin settles on a primary source with an independent cross-read of the same fact (another operator on another domain), or on Polymarket's Conditional Tokens payout vector on Polygon for an adjudicated market. Prediction markets are discovery and optional cross-checks where their terms permit; Kalshi's terms do not permit either use, so Kalshi is never an input.

Mode: offline (frozen fixtures, data as of 2026-10-10). Taxonomy: `config/burnticker/categories.json` (11 categories). The same matrix is served as JSON at `GET /api/burnticker/v1/coverage` and drawn on the trust page.

A **primary** is a first-party source adapter: kind attested-http or on-chain, tier 4 or better, launchable, not an aggregator, not declared cross-read-only, never Kalshi. An **independent cross-read** reads the same fact (`fact` in `config/burnticker/sources.json`) from another operator on another registrable domain. **Hit rate** = readings the source's schedule expected in the 90-day window that one read produced; **latency** = first sighting by the keeper minus the end of the period; **disagreement** = shared periods where the primary and its cross-read differ beyond the fact's tolerance.

Kalshi categories mapped here (Companies, Business) are discovery only: never a settlement input.

## What we cannot settle today

- **No first-party source at all:** World. Nothing in these categories settles on a primary reading; only Polymarket's yes/no markets can, where a tag maps.
- **Primary source without an independent cross-read:** Elections & Politics (`fedreg.finalRules`, `fec.reports`); Science & Space (`ll2.launches`, `noaa.flares`, `jpl.neo`); Entertainment & Culture (`wiki.views`, `steam.players`); Companies (`edgar.8k`, `github.stars`); Health (`openfda.approvals`). One operator's number cannot settle a coin on its own, so these feeds are refused at creation until a second operator's read of the same fact is configured.
- **Settled numbers (scalar rules) in:** Elections & Politics, Science & Space, Entertainment & Culture, Companies, Health, World. Polymarket is binary-only, so where no primary pair exists there is no settled number at all: index closes, rates and commodity settlements (Financial markets), daily temperatures and rainfall (Weather & Climate) and every other Kalshi strike ladder have no replacement today.
- **Elections and votes:** adjudicated-only. They settle on Polymarket's payout vector or not at all; no official results feed is configured.
- **One-shot markets** (one question that resolves once): Polymarket only. No primary source answers an arbitrary question.

## How to read this

- **Independent operator, not independent measurement.** FRED republishes BLS series; the pair catches a broken endpoint, a parser error or a tampered response, not an error in the BLS release itself. The same holds for any mirror.
- **Latency is n/a until the keeper has run.** One read carries one fetch time, not a publication history; the keeper's readings table records the first sighting of every reading, and the live audit uses it once a token reads the source.
- **Zero-filled counts read 100%.** A day without a flare or a launch is a reading of 0, so their hit rate measures the read, not the publisher.
- **Snapshots** (block heights, stars, players) have no publication schedule; their cross-read pairs only reads taken within minutes of each other, which the creation preflight does.
- **Kalshi** is excluded as a primary, as a cross-read and as a venue, whatever any config file says: its Developer Agreement and Data Terms forbid settling products on its data or redistributing it.
- offline: every dry run reads the source's frozen fixture and its window ends at that fixture's fetch time; Polymarket tags are taken from the taxonomy as written (the live run checks each on Gamma)

## Per league — team coins and matchups

ESPN's scoreboard lists the games (which, when, the next game and the record) and is never a settlement input. Each game settles on **primary A**, the game's on-chain payout where a Polymarket moneyline market exists, else **primary B**, TheSportsDB's final under its commercial licence (`BURNTICKER_THESPORTSDB_KEY`). The game is confirmed by the league's official feed, or by API-Sports where no official feed exists (`BURNTICKER_APISPORTS_KEY`). Without that key the league's cross-read is missing and its coins are refused at creation.
